concept.tagline: Reuse GPU KV-cache tensors across prompts sharing system instructions, few-shot examples, or multi-turn history via a Radix Tree.
concept.purpose: Eliminate redundant quadratic prefill compute and cut Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) by sharing immutable KV-cache pages in a reference-counted Radix Tree.

spark.summary: RadixAttention indexes cached GPU KV-cache blocks in a compressed prefix trie (Radix Tree) with LRU eviction, enabling zero-copy prefix sharing across concurrent and sequential LLM requests.
spark.keyTakeaway: To keep serving pipelines predictable under bursty prompts, because causal self-attention only depends on preceding tokens, any two prompts sharing a prefix of N tokens can share the exact same physical GPU KV-cache pages—cutting prefill FLOPs and TTFT by 5x–10x.
spark.byteSummary:
In production LLM workloads—multi-turn chat, RAG pipelines, agent tool-use loops, and few-shot prompting—requests repeatedly share long token prefixes (e.g., a 4,000-token system prompt + tool schema). Recomputing the Key-Value (KV) tensors for those prefix tokens on every request wastes massive GPU HBM bandwidth and inflates Time-To-First-Token (TTFT).

RadixAttention (pioneered in SGLang and vLLM Automatic Prefix Caching) replaces per-request ephemeral KV buffers with a persistent **Radix Tree (compressed prefix trie)** in GPU HBM. Each edge represents a sequence of token IDs pointing to physical PagedAttention KV blocks, annotated with a reference count (`ref_count`) and last-access timestamp.

When a new prompt arrives, the scheduler traverses the Radix Tree to find the longest matching prefix in O(prompt_len), increments `ref_count` on those shared physical pages (zero-copy!), and only runs prefill compute on the divergent user suffix. Completed pages with `ref_count == 0` remain cached in HBM and are evicted lazily via leaf-first LRU only when GPU memory is needed.

learningJourney.title: Why Identical Token Prefixes Produce Bit-Identical KV Tensors
learningJourney.purpose: Exploit causal Transformer prefix invariance so requests sharing a prompt prefix reuse identical KV tensors.

explanation.foundation: In a causal decoder-only Transformer, token `i`'s Key and Value vectors (`K_i, V_i`) depend strictly on tokens `0..i` and never on tokens `> i`.
explanation.core: Therefore, if Request A and Request B share an identical prefix of 2,048 tokens (with identical LoRA adapter and positional encoding), their first 2,048 KV vectors are mathematically identical—allowing 100% zero-copy reuse.
explanation.deepDive: In production deployments of AI/LLM Prefix Caching & RadixAttention (Zero-Copy KV Sharing), watch how why identical token prefixes produce bit-identical kv tensors interacts with tail latency, retry amplification, and partial failures. Production RadixAttention systems combine tenant-salted Radix Trees, LPF-with-aging schedulers, 16-token block alignment, and async CPU DRAM offloading.

learningJourney.title: Compressed Prefix Trie Mapping Token Edges to Physical KV Pages
learningJourney.purpose: Index cached token spans in a compressed Radix Tree that splits edges dynamically when new prompts diverge.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Compressed Prefix Trie Mapping Token Edges to Physical KV Pages** as the intuition layer for AI/LLM Prefix Caching & RadixAttention (Zero-Copy KV Sharing): Index cached token spans in a compressed Radix Tree that splits edges dynamically when new prompts diverge.
explanation.core: Each node in the Radix Tree represents a contiguous span of cached tokens mapped to fixed-size GPU KV pages (e.g., 16 tokens/page). When a new prompt diverges mid-edge (e.g., matching 1,000 of 1,500 tokens on an edge), the engine **splits the edge** at token 1,000 into a shared parent node and two child branches—without copying any GPU tensors.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, compressed prefix trie mapping token edges to physical kv pages becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Production RadixAttention systems combine tenant-salted Radix Trees, LPF-with-aging schedulers, 16-token block alignment, and async CPU DRAM offloading.

learningJourney.title: Reference Counting & Leaf-First LRU Eviction
learningJourney.purpose: Protect active generations with reference counting and reclaim HBM via leaf-first LRU eviction.

explanation.foundation: Active requests pin their matched prefix path by incrementing `ref_count += 1` on every ancestor node, preventing eviction mid-generation. When a request finishes, `ref_count` decrements.
explanation.core: Only **leaf nodes** with `ref_count == 0` sit in the LRU eviction queue; evicting a leaf frees its KV pages and may turn its parent into an evictable leaf.
explanation.deepDive: In production deployments of AI/LLM Prefix Caching & RadixAttention (Zero-Copy KV Sharing), watch how reference counting & leaf-first lru eviction interacts with tail latency, retry amplification, and partial failures. Production RadixAttention systems combine tenant-salted Radix Trees, LPF-with-aging schedulers, 16-token block alignment, and async CPU DRAM offloading.

learningJourney.title: Implementing Longest-Prefix Match & Node Splitting
learningJourney.purpose: Implement longest-prefix matching and mid-edge node splitting in the RadixPrefixCache.

explanation.deepDive:
def match_prefix(self, prompt_tokens: tuple[int, ...]) -> tuple[list[int], int, list[RadixNode]]:
        if not prompt_tokens:
            return [], 0, []
        node = self.root
        idx = 0
        matched_pages: list[int] = []
        pinned_nodes: list[RadixNode] = []
        while idx < len(prompt_tokens):
            first_tok = prompt_tokens[idx]
            child = node.children.get(first_tok)
            if child is None:
                break
            common = 0
            limit = min(len(child.tokens), len(prompt_tokens) - idx)
            while common < limit and child.tokens[common] == prompt_tokens[idx + common]:
                common += 1
            if common < len(child.tokens):
                # Partial edge match: caller stops at split boundary
                break
            matched_pages.extend(child.kv_page_ids)
            child.ref_count += 1
            pinned_nodes.append(child)
            idx += common
            node = child
        return matched_pages, idx, pinned_nodes
```

learningJourney.title: Longest-Prefix-First Scheduling vs. FCFS Starvation
learningJourney.purpose: Prevent LRU cache thrashing with Longest-Prefix-First (LPF) scheduling bounded by starvation limits.

explanation.foundation: In a busy queue, FCFS execution can thrash the LRU cache if unrelated prompts interleave. **Longest-Prefix-First (LPF)** scheduling batches requests sharing the same active Radix branch together, maximizing KV reuse.
explanation.core: To prevent starvation of unique prompts, pair LPF with an **aging boost** so requests waiting > `max_wait_ms` promote to the front.
explanation.deepDive: In production deployments of AI/LLM Prefix Caching & RadixAttention (Zero-Copy KV Sharing), watch how longest-prefix-first scheduling vs. fcfs starvation interacts with tail latency, retry amplification, and partial failures. Production RadixAttention systems combine tenant-salted Radix Trees, LPF-with-aging schedulers, 16-token block alignment, and async CPU DRAM offloading.

learningJourney.title: Page-Boundary Alignment & Tiered CPU-DRAM Offloading
learningJourney.purpose: Extend KV capacity beyond GPU HBM by offloading cold leaf pages asynchronously to CPU DRAM over PCIe.

explanation.foundation: PagedAttention aligns KV blocks to fixed sizes (e.g., 16 tokens). Partial trailing tokens (< 16) are either recomputed or padded at system-prompt boundaries.
explanation.core: When GPU HBM fills, hot evicted KV pages can asynchronously offload over PCIe/NVLink to **CPU DRAM (L2 KV Cache)** rather than discarding them, reloading 5x faster than cold prefill.
explanation.deepDive: In production deployments of AI/LLM Prefix Caching & RadixAttention (Zero-Copy KV Sharing), watch how page-boundary alignment & tiered cpu-dram offloading interacts with tail latency, retry amplification, and partial failures. Production RadixAttention systems combine tenant-salted Radix Trees, LPF-with-aging schedulers, 16-token block alignment, and async CPU DRAM offloading.

learningJourney.title: Preventing Cross-Tenant Cache Leaks & Timing Side Channels
learningJourney.purpose: Eliminate cross-tenant TTFT timing side channels by salting Radix roots with tenant and model identity.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Preventing Cross-Tenant Cache Leaks & Timing Side Channels** as the intuition layer for AI/LLM Prefix Caching & RadixAttention (Zero-Copy KV Sharing): Eliminate cross-tenant TTFT timing side channels by salting Radix roots with tenant and model identity.
explanation.core: Sharing a global Radix Tree without tenant isolation exposes a subtle **TTFT timing side channel**: Tenant B can probe whether Tenant A recently sent a secret system prompt by measuring faster TTFT on a cache hit! Always salt every Radix Tree root or block hash with `tenant_id` (and `lora_id`) so cross-tenant sharing is strictly disabled.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, preventing cross-tenant cache leaks & timing side channels becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Production RadixAttention systems combine tenant-salted Radix Trees, LPF-with-aging schedulers, 16-token block alignment, and async CPU DRAM offloading.

cards.label: TTFT Probe Attack

cards.detail: Keying Radix roots by (tenant_id, model_version, lora_id) makes cross-tenant sharing impossible.

cards.label: Quota Enforcement
cards.detail: Per-tenant HBM soft caps prevent one tenant's 32K prompts from evicting everyone else's caches.

beginner.summary: Prefix Caching saves the AI model's processed memory for common system prompts so new user questions skip re-reading the same instructions.
beginner.keyTakeaway: To keep serving pipelines predictable under bursty prompts, because causal self-attention only depends on preceding tokens, any two prompts sharing a prefix of N tokens can share the exact same physical GPU KV-cache pages—cutting prefill FLOPs and TTFT by 5x–10x.
beginner.byteSummary:
Imagine giving an AI a 4,000-word handbook before every question. Normally, the GPU re-reads that entire handbook for every single user.

RadixAttention stores the processed handbook in a prefix tree so every new question reuses it instantly and only reads the new user message.

intermediate.summary: RadixAttention organizes PagedAttention KV blocks in a reference-counted Radix Tree with leaf-first LRU eviction and longest-prefix matching.
intermediate.keyTakeaway: To keep serving pipelines predictable under bursty prompts, because causal self-attention only depends on preceding tokens, any two prompts sharing a prefix of N tokens can share the exact same physical GPU KV-cache pages—cutting prefill FLOPs and TTFT by 5x–10x.
intermediate.byteSummary:
Because causal attention is prefix-invariant, identical leading tokens produce identical KV tensors. A Radix Tree indexes token spans to physical GPU pages.

Requests pin matched paths (`ref_count > 0`) during execution, and idle leaves evict via LRU.

advanced.summary: Production RadixAttention systems combine tenant-salted Radix Trees, LPF-with-aging schedulers, 16-token block alignment, and async CPU DRAM offloading.
advanced.keyTakeaway: To keep serving pipelines predictable under bursty prompts, because causal self-attention only depends on preceding tokens, any two prompts sharing a prefix of N tokens can share the exact same physical GPU KV-cache pages—cutting prefill FLOPs and TTFT by 5x–10x.
advanced.byteSummary:
At multi-tenant scale, RadixAttention requires strict `tenant_id` key salting to eliminate TTFT timing side channels. Pairing Longest-Prefix-First scheduling with wait-time aging maximizes HBM hit rates without starving tail traffic.

Offloading evicted GPU pages asynchronously to CPU DRAM extends effective prefix capacity across PCIe.
